This morning, Iskandar had awoken earlier than usual. There were several hours yet until daylight. He thought to wake the children early, that they might have more time to work on their smithing skills, but he hesitated to disturb them, and went to warm the forge on his own. "Let them rest this day," he thought to himself. "They will have many days yet to spend studying." He pumped the bellows slowly, and enjoyed the quiet of the forge before the work began.

In the nearby Temple of Cruxius, within the Halls of Flux, Quadrivus worked to trim the branches of the Primrose Tree. Such a duty was usually left to the younger apprentices, but all of the Order of Flux found themselves drawn to the task at times as a way to clear their minds and contemplate. It was a relaxing task, and in the darkness of the pre-dawn, Quadrivus found himself pondering the words Lord Cruxius had spoken to him. The forgemaster, Iskandar, was to be given a crystal of power, formed into a sort of cone shape, that was to be infused with the moonfire their race had discovered and a single mote of the strange "dust of creation". Acquiring the crystal had been simple, but the shaping and infusing of the crystal was a different matter. Beneath the Halls of Flux, where the more...private, projects were often taken, Quadrivus had tasked his brightest with the creation of the Crystal. When envoys had come from the Order of the Moon asking for assistance on another project, he had enlisted their help in its creation as well, for surely the knowledge could be put to use again.

Lost in thought as he was, Quadrivus never saw the creature walk into the Temple until she suddenly stood behind the Tree. "For not being a god of nature," she said, "he sure does love his Tree." Quadrivus jumped at the interruption of the silence. He stepped back, composed himself, and tried to figure out what the creature was. From its back spanned 8 massive arachnid-like legs, many of which were engaged in holding a large, almost obsidian-looking barrel behind her, though it's face and body looked more like a young Thorac [](#s "(i.e. Human)") female. "You must be Quadrivus," she spoke again. "Lord Cruxius said I would find you here. I'm here to retrieve the crystal for the forging of his Hammer. Be a dear and fetch it for me." She set down the barrel gingerly and sat atop it.

[](#s "The hellites have been around since creation, so I assume their mental capacity is vast as well. Quadrivus, in this case, has never been face-to-face with a creature with a mind as old as a hellite's, and so I'm just taking some poetic liberties with explaining what that must be like.") Quadrivus sensed from her mind a certainty of purpose, but trying to read anything more seemed a monolithic task, as if he were trying to carry of bucket of water in a thimble. He wasn't sure how he felt about this... "Welcome to the temple, my dear. If Lord Cruxius himself has sent you, then I will gladly aid you, but who are you, and of what crystal do you speak?"

Vakni sighed heavily. She stood and walked towards Quadrivus. "You may call me Vakni, Quadrivus. I do not have time for games, but I do have one last task to complete. Would you like to see the Crossroads, Quadrivus?" She pulled a key from her pack and showed it to Quadrivus. "Come, quickly. I haven't time for further delay." She motioned with the key in the air, as if she were unlocking a door only she could see, and suddenly a portal opened before him. "Well, come on then. I still need to grab a paving stone anyways." Quadrivus followed her hesitantly through the portal.

Around him were wonders. A forest of the divine tree, flowing like an ocean into the distance, vast swaths of woods expanding far beyond what seemed possible. Beneath his feet was a golden road, paved as if in the light of the sun itself. Stretching in to the distance, the road seemed as veins in the massive body of the woods themselves, flowing with golden light. The sky above looked as if it were from a dream. Colors and shapes floated through the air, an impossible sight, like the universe in paint upon the waves. Surely this was the Crossroads. Vakni reached onto the edge of the road and began prying at a golden stone with a small blade. She pried loose one of the golden stones and returned to his side. "Do we have an understanding now, Quadrivus?" She handed him the stone, which felt warm in his hands, and motioned for him to step back through the portal. As she followed him through, she closed the portal behind herself. "Now, the crystal?"

Quadrivus stared blankly at her for a moment and then gazed back at the stone in his hands. Still it held warmth, and still it glowed as if in broad daylight. He reluctantly handed the stone to Vakni. "I will fetch it for you myself, straight away."

The others in the temple stared at Vakni, and at the empty air where she and Quadrivus had disappeared and reappeared from only moments ago. They would share with all their friends in the Order of Flux of the time they saw a glimpse of the Crossroads, and the servant of Cruxius who walked between the worlds. Vakni sat back on the barrel and took from her pack several primrose berries and a flask. She had grown fond of the flavor, though she knew better than to eat them without having aqua animi at hand. As she snacked on the berries, the spectra in the temple remained silent, unsure if they should move. Vakni attempted to ignore them. She tossed a berry into the air and attempted to catch it in her mouth, as she had seen Cruxius do a thousand times lately, and missed. Embarrassed, she turned to the surrounding crowd, which grew larger as more slowly wandered into the temple. "Don't you people have something you should be doing?" she huffed. The crowd slowly dissipated, hushed whispers filtering through the halls as the spectra attempted to go about their duties. A few brave spectra came forward and asked to touch the stone that Vakni carried, which she tolerated.

After a short time, Quadrivus returned to the temple with a page, who carried a small, unassuming crate. "Here is the package Lord Cruxius demanded," he whispered quietly. Quadrivus' gaze often returned to the paving stone as he spoke. "We have prepared the barrels of aqua animi to the forgemaster's specification as well, and have them ready if you have need."

Vakni pried open the edge of the crate to peer inside. She wasn't sure what magic she was expecting, but the crystal, which glowed slightly in the box, appeared to be in order. "Good. Gather your most promising students and masters of moonfire and meet me in the Forge of Roxxarum. Bring the barrels and the dust, as well." She turned, shifting the crate and the stone into the crook of her arm, and pulled the key from her pocket. She gingerly retrieved the barrel she had been sitting on, and held it fast in the many arms the sprouted from her back. "Tonight, Quadrivus," she said, as the portal opened before her, "you will witness the creation of a legend."

With that she stepped through the portal and vanished. Quadrivus hesitated only a moment, gazing longingly as the air where he had seen, for the second time that night, the Crossroads themselves. He turned, and with the air of authority of the leader of the Order of Flux, gathered his forces. Rumour spread quickly about the encounter, and how Quadrivus had walked upon the Crossroads. Those who had touched the stone would find, in the coming days, that where their hands had brushed upon the stone, a faint, golden glow could be seen. Quadrivus alone had grasped the stone fully, and he would come to be known in history as the Golden Saint, for as he aged the glow spread through his form, visible night or day, Cruxius smiled to himself. He had a flair for the dramatic.

As daylight crested the horizon and glowed upon the crystal tower, 15 exhausted mages exited the temple of Roxxarum. They took with them several barrels, and returned to the Halls of Flux. As the final barrel was wheeled out, Iskandar's apprentices and friends from his journey to Sentenza gathered before the temple. The doors stood open before them at the top of the stairs, and Iskandar stood silently in the entryway holding something covered in a long, leather sheet. "Long have we journeyed," he began, "to find a place that called to us from across Gaea. A home. On this day, in the temple of Roxxarum in the Free City of Sentenza, I have forged for us a commemoration of our new home, our new beginning, our genesis as a free people in the Heavy Lands. Behold! The Hammer of Genesis!" Iskandar tore back the sheet and raised forth the Hammer. As he did so, a massive gout of brilliant moonfire shot from the head of the hammer and into the sky above, surprising even Iskandar with its display. As the fire died down, the gathered Holnareem cheered for the forgemaster, and for their new home. Iskandar tried to share the hammer with his apprentices, that they might feel how light and powerful the great treasure felt, but found that none could lift it from where it lay. Even the strongest of the Holnareem who had journeyed with them could not remove the Hammer once Iskandar set it down, but when he reached for the Hammer, he found it lighter than he expected such a massive hammer to be. Many prayed to Roxxarum that day, and story spread amongst them of the forgemaster chosen to wield the magical Hammer that Roxxarum had gifted him.
